craft_notes: Sthāyin: unhedged-giving (everything — village to kin — may be given to the devoted). Rows: row 1 (list uncut — the ladder from land to kin). Close: kin (the nearest closes: hardest gift last). Rejected: 'renunciation' — killed: given kept (dāna as giving-to, not giving-up); trimming the list — killed: village-kingdom-town-country-son-wife-kin kept whole (the totality IS the unhedgedness).

lines: To devotees, guru's company: given unhedged:
village, kingdom, town, country, son, wife, kin.
l4.sanskrit_cite: bhaktānāṃ guruvargasya dātavyaṃ nirviśaṅkayā | grāmo rājyam puraṃ deśaḥ putradārakuṭumbakam

reads_against.argmap: What may be given to the devoted? → Everything — kingdom and family — may be given to the guru's devoted without hesitation.
c1_essence: Everything given to devotees without hesitation.
